title: [Bug]: milvus-standalone docker crashing
body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

### Environment

```markdown
Using https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus/blob/master/scripts/standalone_embed.sh to install and start standalone milvus in docker container.

Using Milvus v2.6.9:

6d0207bf90a3   milvusdb/milvus:v2.6.9                            "/tini -- milvus run…"   5 days ago      Up Less than a second (health: starting)   0.0.0.0:2379->2379/tcp, [::]:2379->2379/tcp, 0.0.0.0:9091->9091/tcp, [::]:9091->9091/tcp, 0.0.0.0:19530->19530/tcp, [::]:19530->19530/tcp   milvus-standalone

Container falls into restart loop with crashing.
```

docker container to start properly

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
This is what Gemini is telling:
You are running Milvus Standalone (which runs an embedded Etcd for metadata). The error indicates that the persisted data (stored on your disk) from a previous run is in an inconsistent state or corrupt. When Milvus starts, it tries to recover the old Etcd state, but the internal "leader" election fluctuates, causing the initialization process to panic.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: So it seems that standalone version is not properly handling OOM cases or OS crash.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
The Crash will return: The reason we had to move it was that the database file inside it was corrupted or so bloated that it caused the request timed out panic.
The Metadata (The "Brain"): Stored in Etcd. This contains the names of your collections, their schemas, and exactly which files on disk belong to which collection.

It seems that there is unsafe state saving. DB file is corrupted.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
Seems @#43682 and @#36648 hit the same failure chain. The pattern seems to be: unclean shutdown -> bbolt dirty pages not flushed -> etcd won't start -> deleting /var/lib/milvus/etcd to recover -> all collection metadata gone. Vector files in MinIO survive physically but are orphaned because Milvus no longer knows they exist. Without a recent snapshot, that's effectively permanent data loss.

I looked at how others handle this: both Qdrant and Weaviate eliminated the external catalog dependency entirely. Qdrant runs native Raft consensus inside its own binary, so no etcd, no separate process, no split failure domain. Weaviate does the same for all collection/shard metadata through an embedded Raft implementation. In both cases, metadata writes are quorum-committed, so a SIGKILL on any single node cannot produce catalog loss because surviving nodes hold the replicated state.

- Is there a roadmap plan to address the Standalone embedded etcd single-point-of-failure, either through a native Raft-based metadata store (like Qdrant/Weaviate) or a better-supported lightweight external-etcd path?

- Woodpecker seems a great improvement for the ingestion WAL - is there similar plan for the metadata catalog layer?

- It would be good to have for now preStop hook or graceful shutdown guarantee to ensure bbolt is flushed before the container exits.

The etcd durability risk makes it hard to confidently run Milvus (without making deliberate mitigations) in environments where OOM events, maintenance windows and pod scheduling are routine.

I really hope to recover my data, and I had made a backup of the whole "volumes" dir when I insert about 1/4 data. LLM's wrongly fix to delete my the etcd in "volumes", and so I use the backed "volumes" which has the etcd. I let LLM to write a retry loop to check docker status and run "bach standalone_embed.sh start" if status is not healthy, after about one hundred auto retries, it suddenly is ok to start the milvus successfuly. Now, I get about 1/4 indexed data recover. 
Why is there a very rare case to start successfuly? could someone share views? thanks in advance!!

reply by codex 5.3
```
Most likely: you hit a startup race bug in Milvus v2.6.9 embedded etcd, and retries eventually landed on a “good timing window.”
Evidence from your log:
milvus-start-error.log
Lines 86-94
{"msg":"... became leader at term 30"}panic: etcdserver: leader changed
and again:
milvus-start-error.log
Lines 1859-1867
{"msg":"... became leader at term 31"}panic: etcdserver: leader changed
That pattern means:
etcd is still in leader transition during bootstrap,
mixcoord session init does a read/watch,
the request returns leader changed,
Milvus panics and exits (134), then your script retries.
Why it can succeed after many retries:
This is timing-sensitive (race-like), not deterministic corruption every time.
Each restart slightly changes scheduling/timing (CPU, IO, raft ticks), so eventually startup order avoids the panic window.
Your retry loop (docker rm + start) keeps giving new attempts until one passes.
```

> > > > 遇到了同样的问题，standalone版的milvus在I/O抖动下心跳无法及时响应，触发leader切换，最终panic： etcdserver： leader changed导致进程abort，panic时 WAL写入不一致状态，导致重启也失败。最终损失了所有了etcd数据，同时导致向量数据也编程了孤立文件也无效了。怎么才能防止这种情况的发生？
> > 
> > 
> > 你需要ssd磁盘，然后你etcd和数据放在一块盘上么？这块util有多少？可以考虑把etcd放在其他盘上
> 
> 是在一块盘上，发生故障时util我没记录，当前空闲util 只有0.2%。 以及，如果我把 Milvus拆成独立的etcd + minio + milvus三容器部署会好一些吗？

主要看盘，你是内存索引还是磁盘索引，磁盘索引query会把io打得很高。
